per_question_results.question: What catalyst was used in the Suzuki-Miyaura coupling for preparing Compound 3b?

The palladium catalyst $\text{Pd(PPh}_3\text{)}_4$ (at 5 mol %) was utilized in the microwave-assisted Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction for the preparation of Compound 3b.

- **Assay Protocol / Conditions:** Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling conducted in 1,4-dioxane/$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (4:1 v/v) using $\text{Pd(PPh}_3\text{)}_4$ (5 mol %) as catalyst and $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ (2.0 equiv) as base, heated at 85 °C under argon for 5 h.
- **Manuscript Reference:** Page 2, Section: Chemistry & Synthesis; Page 3, Table 1

The synthesis of the lead 2,4-diaminopyrimidine derivative Compound 3b involved a penultimate chloro intermediate undergoing a Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction with 4-methoxyphenylboronic acid. The transformation was mediated by the palladium catalyst tetrakis(triphenylphosphine)palladium(0) ($\text{Pd(PPh}_3\text{)}_4$) in the presence of potassium carbonate ($\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$) serving as the base in an aqueous 1,4-dioxane solvent system. This synthetic route delivered Compound 3b in an 82% isolated yield as an off-white crystalline solid. Pharmacologically, Compound 3b demonstrated potent ATP-competitive inhibition against recombinant human EGFR kinase, displaying marked superiority over parent unsubstituted analogues and comparable activity to the clinical standard Erlotinib, driven structurally by the introduction of the C-5 ethoxy substituent.
